# Home
## Why I Am Running
🔹 Leadership is not about politics.
🔹 It’s about solving problems.
🔹 It’s about listening to residents, working together, and delivering results.
🔹 I am an engineer, a builder, and a community volunteer who has lived and raised a family in Fremont for 30 years.
🔹 I am not a career politician.
🔹 I believe in practical solutions, fiscal responsibility, and putting residents first.
🔹 We want a Fremont that has safe and vibrant neighborhoods, thriving families, and where everyone has a fair opportunity to succeed.
🔹 I ask for your support to help build a stronger Fremont—together.
At the end of the day, we are Fremont, and Fremont is for the people!
Ying-Min Li
Candidate, Fremont City Council District 4
## My Experience and Leadership
I have founded multiple businesses, spent many years in business operations and capital investment, and been deeply involved in nonprofit leadership. I come from both Silicon Valley’s high-tech industry and years of hands-on city and community development. I bring experience in business, technology, and public service.
Years of managing organizations and serving the community have taught me how to make clear, responsible choices in complex situations:
- Spend public money where it truly makes a difference
- Make balanced decisions that benefit the entire community
- Take responsibility for the future—not just the next election
Through my long involvement in Fremont’s public and nonprofit sectors, working closely with residents, volunteers, and city agencies, I see not just numbers on paper—but how policies truly affect families, safety, neighborhoods, and quality of life.
I know that every inefficient policy in Fremont ultimately means higher taxes and worse public services for residents. And I know what kinds of decisions will make our city safer, more efficient, more inclusive, and more livable.
## My Priorities
These are my priorities for the City of Fremont.
### Improve
Traffic Efficiency
- Restore vehicle capacity on major corridors by re-evaluating high-impact bike lanes
- Deploy smart traffic signals to improve traffic flow
- Employ targeted intersection redesign and road resurfacing
### Safe
Neighborhoods
- Support strong law enforcement and firm consequences for home break-ins, vehicle theft, and violent crime
- Expand rehabilitation and re-entry programs for non-violent, first-time offenders
- Safe, clean and well-maintained parks & playgrounds for children, seniors and families
### Addressing Homelessness
- Focus on early intervention to prevent residents from becoming unhoused
- Ensure access to mental health care, medical services, and job support for those in shelters
### Local Business
Growth
- Revitalize neighborhood shopping and services
